AMD delivers record quarter as Data Center segment revenue grows 97% year-over-year, driven by record sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ:AMD) today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2026. Third quarter revenue was $13.4 billion, gross margin was 54%, operating income was $2.8 billion, net income was $2.4 billion and diluted earnings per share was $1.46. On a non-GAAP(*) basis, gross margin was 56%, operating income was $3.9 billion, net income was $3.5 billion and diluted earnings per share was $2.09.

"We delivered a record quarter with revenue exceeding the high end of our guidance as Data Center segment sales nearly doubled year-over-year," said Dr. Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO. "Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and 'Venice' production. With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years."

"Third quarter revenue grew 45% year-over-year to a record $13.4 billion, while non-GAAP earnings per share grew 74%, demonstrating the significant operating leverage in our business model as our Data Center business drives scale," said Jean Hu, AMD executive vice president, chief financial officer and treasurer. "Our fourth-quarter outlook reflects accelerating revenue and earnings growth, driven by strong demand across our Data Center portfolio."

Segment Summary

Data Center segment revenue was a record $8.5 billion, up 97% year-over-year, driven by strong demand for AMD EPYC™ processors and the launch of AMD Instinct™ MI450 Series GPUs.

Client and Gaming segment revenue was $3.7 billion, down 8% year-over-year. Client business revenue was $2.9 billion, up 7% year-over-year, driven by sales of AMD Ryzen™ mobile processors. Gaming business revenue was $773 million, down 40% year-over-year, due to lower semi-custom and graphics revenue.

Embedded segment revenue was $1.1 billion, up 29% year-over-year, led by growth in aerospace and defense, automotive, communications and industrial end markets.

Delivered total revenues in Q3 2026 of approximately $3.66 billion, exceeding guidance of $3.3 billion while growing 58.5%, the highest year-over-year revenue growth since our IPO.

In partnership with AMD, Arm, Broadcom, d-Matrix, Meta, Microsoft, and Qualcomm, Arista launched open standards-based rack-scale architectures for scale-up and scale-out AI networks.

In September 2026, Arista was added to the S&P 100, an index comprised of 100 major blue-chip companies across multiple industry groups.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., November 03, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Arista Networks, Inc. (NYSE: ANET), an industry leader in data-driven, client-to-cloud networking for large AI, data center, campus, and routing environments, today announced financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

"Arista registered another momentous quarter with the highest year-over-year revenue growth since our IPO and record profitability, surpassing even my high expectations," stated Jayshree Ullal, Chairperson and CEO of Arista Networks. "This strong momentum across customer sectors highlights our increased relevance for the generative and agentic AI era."

Third Quarter Financial Highlights

Revenue of $3.66 billion, an increase of 20.5% compared to the second quarter of 2026, and an increase of 58.5% from the third quarter of 2025.

GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 44.9% and 49.1%, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP operating margin of 42.4% and 48.6% in the third quarter of 2025.

GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.22 and $1.20, respectively, compared to GAAP and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $0.67 and $0.77 in the third quarter of 2025.

A reconciliation of the company's non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP measures has been provided in the financial statement tables included in this press release.

Commenting on the company's financial performance, Chantelle Breithaupt, CFO, said, "This quarter brought a true trifecta for our company, setting new record highs in revenue growth, net income, and EPS. I'm incredibly proud of the Arista team for their hard work in driving such outstanding performance for our shareholders."

Company Highlights

Arista announced open Ethernet rack-scale architectures for scale-up and scale-out AI fabrics – The new liquid-cooled portfolio leverages Ethernet for Scale-Up Networks (ESUN) and introduces the Etherlink™ SU-144 architecture, supporting up to 144 accelerators per rack in a single hop and scaling up to 1,024 XPUs via cross-rack topologies.

Arista detailed its scale-across networking strategy for distributed AI fabrics – Highlighting the flagship Arista 7800 AI Spine and unified Arista EOS®, the company outlined how Segment Routing over IPv6 (SRv6) multiplane forwarding, deterministic routing, and real-time congestion signaling enable lossless, high-radix AI fabrics across geographically distributed data centers up to one million XPUs.

Arista expanded AI-driven software security across its development lifecycle – Collaborating with the likes of Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, Arista embedded domain-specific AI harnesses that accelerate proactive vulnerability discovery, building on the company's track record of low CVEs and no-downtime upgrades.

title: Did The Market Read Cerebras Stock Right?
detail:

Cerebras Systems (CBRS) stock fell 57.6% from August 4 to November 2, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 2.3%. Shares slid following the company's August 12 second-quarter report, and they dropped again in late September and early October as reports said Cerebras lost an OpenAI workload to Nvidia. The price appears to assume Cerebras's growth is less secure than it looked, so how much of that growth depends on OpenAI?

Much Of Cerebras's Backlog Comes From OpenAI

A large part of the business Cerebras has already signed depends on OpenAI. The company had $25.4 billion of contracted work still to deliver at June 30. On the August 12 call, management said none of it came from AWS or any other large cloud provider. September news reports said a significant amount of that backlog traces to a December agreement with OpenAI.

Management said on that same call that OpenAI will still be a meaningful portion of revenue in 2027, and that share will shrink over time as AWS and other customers grow.

The late-September news concerned the customer behind much of that backlog. News reports that week, including on October 2, said Cerebras lost a key workload for OpenAI's Ultrafast mode to Nvidia during the same week a lockup on early holders' shares expired. On October 5, OpenAI's chief executive called Cerebras a close partner, and the shares rose 11% in early trading. They still lost 42.1% between October 2 and November 2. Late in October, short seller Culper Research disclosed a position against Cerebras, and the shares fell 11.7% to a record low on November 2.

Cerebras Reported A Far Wider Loss In August

The losses have not narrowed yet. Cerebras reported revenue of $180 million for the quarter ended June 30, up from $103 million a year earlier but below the $193 million reported for the three months to March 31. The company's operating loss grew to $477 million from $15 million in the prior quarter, though management's own core operating loss was far smaller at $33.6 million. Gross margin fell to 14.2% from 44.6% three months earlier. News reports said the shares slumped more than 18% before trading opened on August 13 after the company missed key estimates.

On that core measure, revenue rose 103% to $209.9 million, but management expects weaker third-quarter margins. The company guided core operating margin to minus 25% to minus 23%, against minus 16% in the second quarter. For the full year, management raised its core revenue outlook to $880 million to $890 million. Management also called the third quarter the low point for core gross margin, with an improvement in the fourth as more of its own lower-cost systems come online.
